hn.originalTitle: Message your other Claude Code sessions
hn.sourceOriginalText:
Message your other Claude Code sessions - Claude Code Docs

​ When to use cross-session messaging

Hand over a finding : when one session discovers a breaking change or makes a decision, Claude summarizes it for the session working on the affected area, instead of you re-explaining it there.

Coordinate parallel worktrees : when sessions work the same repository in separate worktrees , Claude can tell the other sessions what landed.

Get status from long-running work : have a migration or test run report back to the session you’re watching, or ask it yourself from there.

Reply across machines : answer a message that arrived from one of your sessions on another machine or on the web. Across machines, Claude can only reply. It can’t start the exchange.

To continue one conversation in another terminal, or share its context with a new session, resume the session

For a coordinated team of sessions Claude spawns and supervises, use agent teams

To watch and steer many sessions from one place, use agent view

To steer a session yourself from your phone or another device, rather than have sessions message each other, use Remote Control

To push external events, such as CI results or chat messages, into a session, use channels

​ Message another session

Ask the session running in my other terminal whether the migration finished Claude writes the actual message itself, so your prompt can leave the content to Claude. This prompt asks for a summary without dictating its wording, and what Claude sends varies: Explain what we just did to the session working on the payments API For what the message Claude writes looks like when it arrives, including an example of one, see what a message looks like . ​ Message delivery The receiving Claude reads the message between tool calls during an active turn, so a running tool is never interrupted. When the receiving session is idle, Claude Code starts a new turn with the message. Between two ordinary inter.

hn.originalTitle: Cloudflare launches Kitesurf, a browser built for AI agents
hn.sourceOriginalText:
Cloudflare launches Kitesurf, a browser built for AI agents | TechCrunch

Cloudflare is the latest company to join the race to build a new web browser. But instead of pitching a Chrome alternative to consumers, the internet infrastructure provider launched Kitesurf , a cloud-hosted browser designed specifically for AI agents.

AI software is evolving from chatbots that answer questions to agents that can complete tasks on users’ behalf. Browsers are a critical part of this transition, as they’ll need to navigate the web and use websites, as humans do.

Unlike traditional web browsers built for humans, a browser built for AI agents doesn’t care about visual elements, like themes, tabs, or browser extensions, Cloudflare explained in its announcement . A browser designed for AI agents needs to manage context windows, performance, token costs, and scalability. It also faces a different threat model because an AI browser could be subject to vulnerabilities like prompt injection attacks and more, the company noted.

With Kitesurf, AI developers will be able to build software that can navigate websites, fill out forms, and complete other browser-based tasks, without having to build their own browser software.

Cloudflare says it decided to build Kitesurf just 12 weeks ago, and it runs entirely on top of the company’s serverless platform, called Workers. Kitesurf is available for free while in beta in Browser Run , which lets developers programmatically control and interact with headless browser instances on Cloudflare’s network.

For developers, Cloudflare’s pitch is that this enables AI agents to use the web more efficiently while using less computing power than Chromium, which keeps costs down.

“Kitesurf is significantly more efficient in CPU and memory consumption than Chromium for common agentic tasks like screenshots and HTML extraction,” according to the company.

The browser itself was built from other technologies, including a modular rendering engine from Blitz ; Firefox’s CSS parser, Stylo ; and Boa JS , a Rust ECMAScript engine. Everything else runs inside Cloudflare Workers. Although still new, Cloudflare says Kitesurf already passes around 215,000+ web platform tests , and it’s adding hundreds more, passing tests every week.

Cloudflare also credited the open source Rust headless engine, Obscura, for inspiring it to develop Kitesurf, noting that the first proof of concept was a port of Obscura to Workers.

The company said the browser correctly renders pages like TodoMVC , a popular benchmark application for comparing JavaScript frameworks, along with Wikipedia, Hacker News, the Cloudflare Blog, and much of the Cloudflare dashboard.

hn.sourceTextZh:
Cloudflare 推出 Kitesurf，一款專為 AI 代理程式打造的瀏覽器 | TechCrunch Cloudflare 是最新一家加入建置新網頁瀏覽器競賽的公司。但這家網路基礎設施供應商並沒有向消費者推銷 Chrome 替代品，而是推出了 Kitesurf，這是一款專為人工智慧代理設計的雲端託管瀏覽器。人工智慧軟體正在從回答問題的聊天機器人發展到可以代表用戶完成任務的代理。瀏覽器是這項轉變的關鍵部分，因為它們需要像人類一樣瀏覽網路並使用網站。 Cloudflare 在其公告中解釋說，與為人類構建的傳統 Web 瀏覽器不同，為 AI 代理構建的瀏覽器並不關心主題、選項卡或瀏覽器擴展等視覺元素。為人工智慧代理設計的瀏覽器需要管理上下文視窗、效能、令牌成本和可擴充性。該公司指出，它還面臨不同的威脅模型，因為人工智慧瀏覽器可能會受到提示注入攻擊等漏洞的影響。借助 Kitesurf，人工智慧開發人員將能夠建立可以導航網站、填寫表格以及完成其他基於瀏覽器的任務的軟體，而無需建立自己的瀏覽器軟體。 Cloudflare 表示，它在 12 週前決定建立 Kitesurf，它完全運行在該公司名為 Workers 的無伺服器平台之上。

Kitesurf 在 Browser Run 的測試版中免費提供，它允許開發人員以程式設計方式控制 Cloudflare 網路上的無頭瀏覽器實例並與之互動。對於開發人員來說，Cloudflare 的主張是，這使人工智慧代理能夠更有效地使用網絡，同時使用比 Chromium 更少的運算能力，從而降低成本。該公司表示：「對於螢幕截圖和 HTML 提取等常見代理任務，Kitesurf 在 CPU 和內存消耗方面比 Chromium 更加高效。」瀏覽器本身是由其他技術構建的，包括來自 Blitz 的模組化渲染引擎； Firefox 的 CSS 解析器 Stylo ；和 Boa JS ，一個 Rust ECMAScript 引擎。其他一切都在 Cloudflare Workers 內運作。儘管還是個新事物，Cloudflare 表示 Kitesurf 已經通過了大約 215,000 多項網路平台測試，並且還在增加數百項測試，每週都會通過測試。 Cloudflare 也稱讚開源 Rust 無頭引擎 Obscura 激勵其開發 Kitesurf，並指出第一個概念驗證是 Obscura 向 Workers 的移植。該公司表示，該瀏覽器可以正確呈現 TodoMVC 等頁面，TodoMVC 是用於比較 JavaScript 框架的流行基準應用程序，以及維基百科、駭客新聞、Cloudflare 部落格和 Cloudflare 儀表板的大部分內容。當您透過我們文章中的連結購買時，我們可能會賺取少量佣金。

hn.originalTitle: Message your other Claude Code sessions
hn.sourceOriginalText:
Message your other Claude Code sessions - Claude Code Docs

​ When to use cross-session messaging

Hand over a finding : when one session discovers a breaking change or makes a decision, Claude summarizes it for the session working on the affected area, instead of you re-explaining it there.

Coordinate parallel worktrees : when sessions work the same repository in separate worktrees , Claude can tell the other sessions what landed.

Get status from long-running work : have a migration or test run report back to the session you’re watching, or ask it yourself from there.

Reply across machines : answer a message that arrived from one of your sessions on another machine or on the web. Across machines, Claude can only reply. It can’t start the exchange.

To continue one conversation in another terminal, or share its context with a new session, resume the session

For a coordinated team of sessions Claude spawns and supervises, use agent teams

To watch and steer many sessions from one place, use agent view

To steer a session yourself from your phone or another device, rather than have sessions message each other, use Remote Control

To push external events, such as CI results or chat messages, into a session, use channels

​ Message another session

Ask the session running in my other terminal whether the migration finished Claude writes the actual message itself, so your prompt can leave the content to Claude. This prompt asks for a summary without dictating its wording, and what Claude sends varies: Explain what we just did to the session working on the payments API For what the message Claude writes looks like when it arrives, including an example of one, see what a message looks like . ​ Message delivery The receiving Claude reads the message between tool calls during an active turn, so a running tool is never interrupted. When the receiving session is idle, Claude Code starts a new turn with the message. Between two ordinary inter.

hn.originalTitle: OpenAI and four rivals just agreed on one standard for AI agents
hn.sourceOriginalText:
OpenAI and four rivals just agreed on one standard for AI agents

The AI race spent two years being about models. This week it moved to the plumbing. On the eve of GPT-5’s first birthday, OpenAI and four rivals published Agent Plugins , an open standard that lets a single agent extension work across competing products.

The pitch is “build once, run anywhere”. Today, every agent tool expects a different folder layout and setup. Agent Plugins replaces that with one package format. It bundles two things developers already use. The first is Model Context Protocol servers , which connect an agent to live tools and data. The second is Agent Skills, reusable sets of instructions. A plugin is just a folder with a small plugin.json file at its root.

Despite the OpenAI billing, this is not an OpenAI product. Vercel initiated the proposal . Representatives from Amazon, Cursor’s maker Anysphere, GitHub, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Vercel then shaped the 1.0 specification. The steering committee has five members: Amazon, Cursor, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Vercel. The project is openly licensed, and its backers say no single company’s roadmap sets its direction.

OpenAI still framed the launch as its own milestone. GPT-5 turns one on 7 August, and the company is marking the week by looking beyond individual models , per 9to5Mac. Its ChatGPT and Codex apps support the format at launch, alongside Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Kiro, and VS Code. The move goes further than OpenAI’s own Codex plugins , which work only inside its tools.

Deliberately small

The standard is narrow on purpose. It defines how a plugin is packaged and found, and little else. Marketplaces, installation, permissions, sandboxing, and trust all stay with each client. That keeps the format easy to adopt. It also leaves the hardest problems unsolved. Deciding whether a plugin is safe to run is still every client’s own job, a live worry after fake Agent Skills slipped past security scanners earlier this year.

Not everyone is convinced. Dax Raad, who builds the SST developer-tools framework, said he was “very much against” it, calling it “a thin standard” whose useful parts will end up in client-specific extensions anyway.

Others cheered. “We neeeeded this,” wrote developer advocate Angie Jones, who had wanted one way to carry her skills between the tools she uses.

The bigger question is what standardising the plumbing does to competition. A shared format could let a small developer reach every major agent at once. That is the open-ecosystem case, and it is a real one. It could also cement the handful of clients that already have the users, because a standard rewards whoever people already run.

For now the plumbing is agreed. The fight over the parts it leaves out, the marketplaces and the trust, has barely started.

hn.titleZh: OpenAI 和四家競爭對手剛剛就人工智慧代理的一項標準達成一致
hn.summaryZh: 這篇來自 Hacker News 工程師討論，重點和 OpenAI / Agent 有關。適合用來快速了解社群正在討論的實作方向、工具變化或使用心得。
hn.sourceTextZh:
OpenAI 和四家競爭對手剛剛就人工智慧代理的一項標準達成一致。人工智慧競賽花了兩年時間圍繞著模型進行。本週它轉移到了管道系統。在 GPT-5 一歲生日前夕，OpenAI 和四個競爭對手發布了 Agent Plugins，這是一個開放標準，允許單一代理商擴展跨競爭產品工作。其宣傳語是「建構一次，隨處運行」。如今，每個代理工具都需要不同的資料夾佈局和設定。代理插件將其替換為一種包格式。它捆綁了開發人員已經使用的兩種東西。第一個是模型上下文協定伺服器，它將代理連接到即時工具和資料。第二個是代理技能，可重複使用的指令集。插件只是一個資料夾，其根目錄下有一個小的plugin.json 檔案。儘管有 OpenAI 計費，但這不是 OpenAI 產品。 Vercel 發起了這項提議。來自亞馬遜、Cursor 製造商 Anysphere、GitHub、微軟、OpenAI 和 Vercel 的代表隨後制定了 1.0 規範。指導委員會有五名成員：Amazon、Cursor、Microsoft、OpenAI 和 Vercel。該計畫已獲得公開許可，其支持者表示，沒有一家公司的路線圖能夠確定其方向。 OpenAI 仍然將此次發布視為自己的里程碑。根據 9to5Mac 報導，GPT-5 將於 8 月 7 日滿歲，該公司將透過超越單一模型來紀念這一周。

其 ChatGPT 和 Codex 應用程式在發佈時支援該格式，此外還有 Cursor、GitHub Copilot、Kiro 和 VS Code。此舉比 OpenAI 自己的 Codex 插件更進一步，後者只能在其工具內部運作。故意縮小 標準有意縮小範圍。它定義了插件的打包和查找方式，僅此而已。市場、安裝、權限、沙箱和信任都保留在每個客戶端身上。這使得該格式易於採用。它還沒有解決最困難的問題。決定插件是否可以安全運行仍然是每個客戶自己的工作，這是今年早些時候假冒代理技能溜過安全掃描儀後的一個令人擔憂的問題。並非所有人都相信。建造 SST 開發人員工具框架的 Dax Raad 表示，他“非常反對”它，稱其為“薄標準”，無論如何，其有用的部分最終都會出現在特定於客戶端的擴展中。其他人歡呼起來。 「我們需要這個，」開發者倡導者 Angie Jones 寫道，她希望有一種方法可以在她使用的工具之間運用她的技能。更大的問題是管道標準化對競爭有何影響。共享格式可以讓小型開發商立即聯繫到每個主要代理商。這就是開放生態系的案例，而且是真實的案例。它還可以鞏固少數已經擁有用戶的客戶，因為標準會獎勵已經運行的人。目前，管道工程已達成協議。

對於它遺漏的部分——市場和信任——的爭奪才剛剛開始。取得 TNW 電子報 每週在您的收件匣中獲取最重要的科技新聞。
